Spatial analyticity of solutions for a coupled system of generalized KdV equations

A. Atmani, A. Boukarou, D. Benterki, and Kh. Zennir Address: Amel Atmani
Department of Mathematics Bordj Bou Arreridj University, Algeria. Email address: amel.atmani@univ-bba.dz Address: Aissa Boukarou
Department of Mathematics, University of Ghardaia, Algeria. Email address: boukarouaissa@gmail.com Address: Djamila Benterki
Department of Mathematics Bordj Bou Arreridj University, Algeria. Email address:benterkidj@yahoo.fr Address: Khaled zennir
Department of Mathematics, College of Sciences and Arts, Qassim University, Ar-Rass, Saudi Arabia Email address:k.zennir@qu.edu.sa
Laboratoire de Mathématiques Appliquées et de Modélisation, Université 8 Mai 1945 Guelma. B.P. 401 Guelma 24000 Algérie.

Abstract. The solution of a coupled system consisting of generalized Korteweg-de Vries-type equations is obtained for all time where the initial data are analytic on a band in the complex plane. We show that the width of this band decreases algebraically with time.

Keywords. Generalized Korteweg–de Vries, well-posedness, Radius of spatial analyticity, Analytic space.

2010 Mathematics Subject Classification. 35E15, 35Q53, 35B65, 35C07.

1. Introduction

This paper deals with the initial-value problem for a coupled system of generalized Korteweg–de Vries (gKdV) equation

{ut+∂x3u+∂x(up​vp+1)=0vt+∂x3v+∂x(up+1​vp)=0,x,t∈ℝ,p∈ℤ+u(x,0)=u0(x),v(x,0)=v0(x),\left\{\begin{array}[]{l}u_{t}+\partial_{x}^{3}u+\partial_{x}\left(u^{p}v^{p+1}\right)=0\\ v_{t}+\partial_{x}^{3}v+\partial_{x}\left(u^{p+1}v^{p}\right)=0,\quad x,t\in\mathbb{R},p\in\mathbb{Z}^{+}\\ u(x,0)=u_{0}(x),\quad v(x,0)=v_{0}(x),\end{array}\right. (1.1)

where the unknown u=u⁡(x,t),v=v⁡(x,t)u=u(x,t),~v=v(x,t) and the initial data(u0​(x),v0​(x))(u_{0}(x),v_{0}(x)) are real-valued.
This type of equation is a special case of an important vast class of nonlinear evolution equations which was studied by M. Ablowitz [1], and it has applications in physical problems, which describes the strong interaction of two dimensional long internal gravity waves.
For p=1p=1, the system can be reduce to a coupled system of modified KdV (mKdV) equations

{ut+∂x3u+∂x(u​v2)=0vt+∂x3v+∂x(u2​v)=0,x,t∈ℝu(x,0)=u0(x),v(x,0)=v0(x).\left\{\begin{array}[]{l}u_{t}+\partial_{x}^{3}u+\partial_{x}\left(uv^{2}\right)=0\\ v_{t}+\partial_{x}^{3}v+\partial_{x}\left(u^{2}v\right)=0,\quad x,t\in\mathbb{R}\\ u(x,0)=u_{0}(x),\quad v(x,0)=v_{0}(x).\end{array}\right. (1.2)

Here, the author proved the local well posdness in in Hs,s≥14H^{s},s\geq\frac{1}{4}. For s≥1s\geq 1, it is proved that the global well posdness is assured. In addition, M. Panthee improved it to extend solution to be in any time interval [0,T][0,T] for s>49s>\frac{4}{9}.
The authors in [14] studied the local well-posdness in (Hs×Hs)(H^{s}\times H^{s}) with s>−12s>-\frac{1}{2} for system consisting modified Korteweg–de Vries-type equations

{ut+∂x3u+∂x(u2​v3)=0,vt+α​∂x3v+∂x(u3​v2)=0,x,t∈ℝu(x,0)=u0(x),v(x,0)=v0(x),\left\{\begin{array}[]{l}u_{t}+\partial_{x}^{3}u+\partial_{x}\left(u^{2}v^{3}\right)=0,\\ v_{t}+\alpha\partial_{x}^{3}v+\partial_{x}\left(u^{3}v^{2}\right)=0,\quad x,t\in\mathbb{R}\\ u(x,0)=u_{0}(x),\quad v(x,0)=v_{0}(x),\end{array}\right. (1.3)

where 0<α<10<\alpha<1 and (u0,v0)(u_{0},v_{0}) is given in low regularity Sobolev spaces(Hs×Hs)(H^{s}\times H^{s}), but if α=1\alpha=1 the authors obtained the local well posedness for s⩾14s\geqslant\frac{1}{4}.
In [2], the problem (1.1)(\ref{p01}) is studied and the local and global well-posedness results with (u0,v0)∈Hs×Hs(u_{0},v_{0})\in H^{s}\times H^{s}, s⩾1s\geqslant 1 and p⩾1p\geqslant 1 is shown. The golobal well-posedness was obtained by using the next conserved quantities satisfied by the flow of (1.1)(\ref{p01})

∫ℝu​𝑑x∫ℝv​𝑑x12​∫ℝu2+v2​𝑑xand12​∫ℝux2+vx2−2p+1​up+1​vp+1​𝑑x.\int_{\mathbb{R}}udx\quad\int_{\mathbb{R}}vdx\quad\frac{1}{2}\int_{\mathbb{R}}u^{2}+v^{2}dx\quad\textit{and}\quad\frac{1}{2}\int_{\mathbb{R}}u_{x}^{2}+v_{x}^{2}-\frac{2}{p+1}u^{p+1}v^{p+1}dx.

In addition, the authors showed the existence and nonlinear stability of the solitary wave solution. The study of stability for solitary wave solution is followed from the abstract results of Grillakis, for more details, please see [3, 4, 17, 21].
For p=2p=2, the system is turn out to a coupled system of modified Korteweg–de Vries (gKdV) equation

{ut+∂x3u+∂x(u2​v3)=0,vt+∂x3v+∂x(u3​v2)=0,x,t∈ℝu(x,0)=u0(x),v(x,0)=v0(x).\left\{\begin{array}[]{l}u_{t}+\partial_{x}^{3}u+\partial_{x}\left(u^{2}v^{3}\right)=0,\\ v_{t}+\partial_{x}^{3}v+\partial_{x}\left(u^{3}v^{2}\right)=0,\quad x,t\in\mathbb{R}\\ u(x,0)=u_{0}(x),\quad v(x,0)=v_{0}(x).\end{array}\right. (1.4)

Panthee and Scialom [19], investigated some well-posedness issues for eq (1.4)(\ref{p07}) in Hs×HsH^{s}\times H^{s}, which proved local and global will posdness for s⩾0s\geqslant 0.
For related problems in analytic Gevrey spaces, we review the results in 2​D2D by M. Shan, L. Zhang [20], where the authors proved that the following problem (the Cauchy problem associated with the 2​D2D generalized Zakharov-Kuznetsov equation)

{ut+(∂x3+∂y3)u+(∂x+∂y)up+1=0,u⁡(0,x,y)=u0​(x,y),\left\{\begin{array}[]{l}u_{t}+(\partial_{x}^{3}+\partial_{y}^{3})u+(\partial_{x}+\partial_{y})u^{p+1}=0,\\ u(0,x,y)=u_{0}(x,y),\end{array}\right. (1.5)

has an analytic solutions in a strip the width, and they gave an algebraic lower bounds.
Bona and Grujić [6] showed the well-posedness of a KdV-type Boussinesq system

{ut+vx+u​ux+vx​x​x=0vt+ux+(u​v)x+ux​x​x=0.\left\{\begin{array}[]{l}u_{t}+v_{x}+uu_{x}+v_{xxx}=0\\ v_{t}+u_{x}+(uv)_{x}+u_{xxx}=0.\end{array}\right. (1.6)

There is another method in this direction, we mention the works by A. Boukarou et al. in the next series of papers [7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 22].
Motivated by the previouse results, we consider our main ptoblem with initial data are analytic on a band in the complex plane and obtained solution for all time. We also showed that the width of this band decreases algebraically with time.
This paper is continuation of our prevouse results and it is structured as follows. In section 11, we give some historical review and motivate this paper to further strengthened, and innovate the main contributions and introduce our main results which we will prove later (local and global well posedness of equation (1.1)). In section 22, we present some definition and the necessary function spaces such as the analytic function spaces 𝒢ρ,s\mathcal{G}_{\rho,s}, analytic Bourgain space Xρ,s,bX_{\rho,s,b} which will be used. In section 33, we prove the Linear and Bilinear Estimates which needed to prove the main results. In section 44, we prove the local and global well-posdness and then obtained lower bound.
We provide a clear, sober and well-written analysis of the problem.

Theorem 1.1.

Let s>32s>\frac{3}{2} and p≥1p\geq 1 and for initial data (u0,v0)∈𝒢ρ,s×𝒢ρ,s(u_{0},v_{0})\in\mathcal{G}_{\rho,s}\times\mathcal{G}_{\rho,s}, ρ>0\rho>0, there exists a positive time TT, such that the initial -value problem (1.1) is well-posed in the space

C⁡([0,T],𝒢ρ,s)×C⁡([0,T],𝒢ρ,s).C\left(\left[0,T\right];\mathcal{G}_{\rho,s}\right)\times C\left(\left[0,T\right];\mathcal{G}_{\rho,s}\right).
Theorem 1.2.

Let ρ0>0\rho_{0}>0 and s>32s>\frac{3}{2} and let T≥t0T\geq t_{0} suppose that the solution uu, vv given by Theorem (1.1)(\ref{the1.2}) extends globally in time. Then, we have

(u,v)∈C⁡([0,2​T],𝒢ρ⁡(T)/2,s)×C⁡([0,2​T],𝒢ρ⁡(T)/2,s),(u,v)\in C([0,2T],\mathcal{G}_{\rho(T)/2,s})\times C([0,2T],\mathcal{G}_{\rho(T)/2,s}),

where ρ⁡(T)\rho(T) is given by

ρ⁡(t)=min⁡{ρ1,K​T−2​p2−6​p−1}.\rho(t)=\min\left\{\rho_{1},KT^{-2p^{2}-6p-1}\right\}.

for some constant K>0K>0.

The u^\widehat{u} is denote the Fourier transform of uu which is defined as

u^​(ζ)=12​π​∫−∞+∞u⁡(x)​e−i​x​ζ​𝑑x.\widehat{u}(\zeta)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\int_{-\infty}^{+\infty}u(x)e^{-ix\zeta}dx.

For a function u⁡(x,t)u(x,t) of two variable we have

u^x​(ζ,t)=12​π​∫−∞+∞u⁡(x,t)​e−i​x​ζ​𝑑x,\widehat{u}^{x}(\zeta,t)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\int_{-\infty}^{+\infty}u(x,t)e^{-ix\zeta}dx,

and

u^​(ζ,η)=12​π​∫−∞+∞∫−∞+∞u⁡(x,t)​e−i​x​ζ​e−i​t​η​𝑑x​𝑑η.\widehat{u}(\zeta,\eta)=\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{-\infty}^{+\infty}\int_{-\infty}^{+\infty}u(x,t)e^{-ix\zeta}e^{-it\eta}dxd\eta.

We note that the operators A,ΛA,\Lambda and FρF_{\rho} are defined as

A​u^​(ζ,η)=(1+|ζ|)​u^​(ζ,η);\widehat{Au}(\zeta,\eta)=\left(1+|\zeta|\right)\widehat{u}(\zeta,\eta);
Λ​u^​(ζ,η)=(1+|η|)​u^​(ζ,η);\widehat{\Lambda u}(\zeta,\eta)=\left(1+|\eta|\right)\widehat{u}(\zeta,\eta);
Fκ^​(ζ,η)=f⁡(ζ,η)(1+|η−ζ3|)κ.\widehat{F_{\kappa}}(\zeta,\eta)=\frac{f(\zeta,\eta)}{\left(1+|\eta-\zeta^{3}|\right)^{\kappa}}.

The mixed Lp−LqL^{p}-L^{q} -norm is defined by

‖u‖Lp​Lq=(∫−∞+∞|∫−∞+∞|u⁡(x,t)|q​𝑑t|pq​𝑑x)1p\|u\|_{L^{p}L^{q}}=\left(\int_{-\infty}^{+\infty}\left|\int_{-\infty}^{+\infty}|u(x,t)|^{q}dt\right|^{\frac{p}{q}}dx\right)^{\frac{1}{p}}

The analytic Gevrey class 𝒢ρ,s\mathcal{G}_{\rho,s} is defined by Foias and Temam [15] as

‖u0‖𝒢ρ,s2=‖eρ⁡(1+|ζ|)​(1+|ζ|)s​u0^​(ζ)‖Lζ2.\left\|u_{0}\right\|_{\mathcal{G}_{\rho,s}}^{2}=\|\mathrm{e}^{\rho(1+|\zeta|)}(1+|\zeta|)^{s}\widehat{u_{0}}(\zeta)\|_{L^{2}_{\zeta}}.

For s,∈ℝs,\in\mathbb{R}, b∈[−1,1]b\in[-1,1] and ρ>0\rho>0, we denote Xρ,s,bX_{\rho,s,b} by ∥⋅∥ρ,s,b\|\cdot\|_{\rho,s,b} with respect to the norm

‖u‖Xρ,s,b=‖eρ⁡(1+|ζ|)​(1+|ζ|)s​(1+|η−ζ3|)b​u^​(ζ,η)‖Lζ,η2.\|u\|_{X_{\rho,s,b}}=\bigg\|e^{\rho(1+|\zeta|)}(1+|\zeta|)^{s}(1+\left|\eta-\zeta^{3}\right|)^{b}\hat{u}(\zeta,\eta)\bigg\|_{L^{2}_{\zeta,\eta}}.

For ρ=0,Xρ,s,b\rho=0,X_{\rho,s,b} coincides with the space Xs,bX_{s,b} introduced by Bourgain [13], and Kenig, Ponce and Vega [18]. The norm of Xs,bX_{s,b} is denoted by ∥⋅∥s,b\|\cdot\|_{s,b}, as follow

‖u‖Xs,b=‖(1+|ζ|)s​(1+|η−ζ3|)b​u^​(ζ,η)‖Lζ,η2.\|u\|_{X_{s,b}}=\bigg\|(1+|\zeta|)^{s}(1+\left|\eta-\zeta^{3}\right|)^{b}\hat{u}(\zeta,\eta)\bigg\|_{L^{2}_{\zeta,\eta}}.

In this section, we shall deduce several estimates to be used in the proof of Theorem (1.1).

supx+i​y∈Sρ−σ|∂xnu⁡(x+i​y)|≤C​‖u‖𝒢ρ,\displaystyle\sup_{\begin{subarray}{c}x+iy\in S_{\rho-\sigma}\end{subarray}}|\partial^{n}_{x}u(x+iy)|\leq C\|u\|_{\mathcal{G}_{\rho}},

Lemma 3.5.

Let b>12b>\frac{1}{2}, b′<−14b^{\prime}<-\frac{1}{4}, and s≥3​bs\geq 3b. Let p∈ℕp\in\mathbb{N} and suppose u1,…,up+1,v1,…,vp+1∈Xρ,s,bu_{1},...,u_{p+1},v_{1},...,v_{p+1}\in X_{\rho,s,b}. Then there exists a constants cc such that

‖∂x∏i=1pui​∏j=1p+1vj‖ρ,s,b′≤C​∏i=1p‖ui‖ρ,s,b.∏j=1p+1‖vj‖ρ,s,b,\|\partial_{x}\prod_{i=1}^{p}u_{i}\prod_{j=1}^{p+1}v_{j}\|_{\rho,s,b^{\prime}}\leq C\prod_{i=1}^{p}\|u_{i}\|_{\rho,s,b}.\prod_{j=1}^{p+1}\|v_{j}\|_{\rho,s,b}, (3.10)

Proof.

First of all, for i=1,2,…,p+1i=1,2,...,p+1 and j=1,2,…,p+1j=1,2,...,p+1, we define

fi​(ζ,η)=(1+|ζ|)s​(1+|η−ζ3|)b​eρ⁡(1+|ζ|)​|ui^​(ζ,η)|\displaystyle f_{i}(\zeta,\eta)=(1+|\zeta|)^{s}(1+|\eta-\zeta^{3}|)^{b}e^{\rho(1+|\zeta|)}|\widehat{u_{i}}(\zeta,\eta)|

The proof is first given for the case p=1p=1, after which the proof for a general 2​p+12p+1 will be more transparent, that means we prove

‖∂xu1​v1​v2‖ρ,s,b′≤C​‖u1‖ρ,s,b​‖v1‖ρ,s,b​‖v2‖ρ,s,b\|\partial_{x}u_{1}v_{1}v_{2}\|_{\rho,s,b^{\prime}}\leq C\|u_{1}\|_{\rho,s,b}\|v_{1}\|_{\rho,s,b}\|v_{2}\|_{\rho,s,b}
